rom.notes: 2012/11/19 [Tactrix] updated to include missing elements. 2024 [Analysis] Extended with additional verified tables from ROM analysis. 2025 [Ghidra H8/539F RE] Added TCU/Transmission category from decompilation of tcu_shift_torque_mgmt @ 0x28fff and isr_sci3_eri @ 0x168e3. 2026-07 [Ghidra RE, session 10] STRUCTURAL FIX: tcu_shift_torque_mgmt was discovered to have been mis-split by Ghidra's auto-analyzer into 4 separate functions (a 2-byte inline data literal at ROM 0x29339-0x2933a, mistaken for code, broke the boundary). It is genuinely ONE function spanning ROM 0x28fff-0x29c31, now renamed tcu_shift_torque_and_knock_mgmt, and it does BOTH TCU shift torque coordination AND per-cylinder knock processing (the latter previously mislabeled as an independent "knock_process_main" with no findable caller). Fixing the boundary immediately surfaced the real caller: isr_sci3_eri (COMPUTED_CALL @ ROM 0x169b1), matching this file's pre-existing note above almost exactly. This also revises the session-3 "two independently-gated subsystems intentionally coordinating via shared f3ac/f3ae" framing to "one function doing both jobs sequentially" - the underlying RAM-register findings (f1f2 bit7 gate, EEC6/EEC8 octane chain, etc.) remain valid, only the two-functions framing changes. Also confirmed this session: the "TCU Shift Torque Cmd Lo/Hi - Per Gear" tables (below) hold raw SCI3 protocol command bytes sent to the TCU, never used in any arithmetic - their existing uint16 "units" scaling is correct as-is; small values (1-2) are expected, not a data error. See logging.txt session 10. Address mapping: XML address = file_offset + 0x10000 Axis RAM pointers: F0C0=RPM, F0C2=Load/MAP, F0C4=CoolantTempA(ADC), F0C6=AirTemp(ADC), F0C8=CoolantTempB(ADC), F0CA=TimeAfterStart, F0CE=ISCVDemand, F0D0=IAT_raw TCU comms: SCI3 serial channel. ECU sends torque cut commands to TCU each crank pulse. tcu_comms_state (RAM 0xf3d0): 0=idle, 1=rx_wait, 2=tx_active tcu_shift_flags (RAM 0xf3cc): bit0=shift_in_progress, bit1=shift_done, bit2=downshift, bit3=upshift, bit5=sport_mode, bit6=torque_cut_suppressed NOTE on throttle_load_pct (RAM 0xf5de): this is computed as crank period delta (T2GR1H - crank_angle_current) in isr_sci3_eri, NOT a TPS voltage reading. It represents engine load derived from crank timing, not pedal position. 2026-07 [Ghidra RE, session 4] CONFIRMED: this ECU has no discrete "knock retard degrees" value (same as Evo 4/5/6 - neither MUT profile exposes one). Knock instead degrades Octane Level (MUT 0x27, RAM 0xEEC8/EEC9, starts at 0xFF=100%) via an intermediate hysteresis counter at RAM 0xEEC6, driven by the knock-sum register (0xF3A2/F3A3). Full confirmed chain: knock_process_main (0x2933b) -> writes knock sum F3A2/F3A3 -> knock_event_counter_update_eec6 (0x251c4): hysteresis vs ROM thresholds 0xB3E/0xB40, drives EEC6 0-255 (up when clean, down under sustained knock) -> octane_level_compute_from_knock_counter (0x252d3): clamps/scales EEC6, writes result to EEC8 = Octane Level Octane Level is what blends between the High/Low-Octane Ignition Maps and Knock Control/Octane Control Above Load tables already defined below - the "retard" is implicit in that map blend, not a standalone logged scalar. A second, independent writer (octane_level_init_or_force_from_ gear_table, 0x24e80) also sets EEC6/EEC8 from a per-gear ROM table at 0x2882 indexed by the current-gear-state variable f1fc, or forces 100% under a separate condition flag (f0fe bit0) - gear-dependent init/override, independent of the knock decay path. Both writers are gated by RAM 0xf1f2 bit7 (same enable bit used for knock-to-TCU torque coordination, see TCU comms note above and logging.txt session 3/4). See logging.txt for full addresses, thresholds, and remaining open threads (undecoded flag bits f1fe.3/f200.0/f0fe.0, ROM table 0x2882 not yet cross-checked against the f1f0/f1f2/f1f4 per-gear config stride).
